entry.evidence: Although these studies have agreed on the lithostratigraphic characteristics of these sedimentary series, there are, however, discrepancies concerning the environment in which they were deposited.

steps.action: States the open question: the depositional environment of the Eocene-Miocene Mrayt Group is disputed among earlier studies.
steps.quote: there are, however, discrepancies concerning the environment in which they were deposited

steps.action: Lists the published rival interpretations: deep-sea fan turbidites (Morley 1992), bottom-current reworked slope sediments on an abyssal plain (Tejera de Leon 1993), and a storm-affected outer-platform prism passing to a deep-sea fan (Raissouni et al. 2008).
steps.quote: synorogenic turbidites organized in two sequences (Morley 1992)

steps.action: Selects five outcrop sections (MG1 to MG5, 1730 m in total) for detailed study and sampling.
steps.quote: Fivesections belonging to the Mrayt Group, totalizing 1730 min thickness has beensubjected to detailed

steps.action: Logs the sections bed by bed at centimetre scale and examines 50 thin sections under a polarizing microscope.
steps.quote: The petrographic study has been based on the examination of 50 thin sections under polarizing microscope

steps.action: Notes that the carbonate content seen in thin section had already been shown in the field by reaction with HCl, a second independent method.
steps.quote: The existence of carbonates had already been demonstrated by the reaction to HCL during the fieldwork.

steps.action: Measures paleocurrents on 48 flute casts and on clast long axes, classifies five mixed petrofacies after Mount (1985), and describes 22 sedimentary facies (F1 to F22).
steps.quote: the recognition for the first time of twenty two sedimentary facies

steps.action: Infers mixed intra-basinal and extra-basinal provenance (sedimentary, volcanic and metamorphic sources plus Cretaceous carbonates), rapid erosion of a high-relief source, and a humid climate from the petrofacies.
steps.quote: suggest a provenance from sedimentary, volcanic and high rank metamorphic sources

steps.action: Rejects in situ biological micritization and burial compaction as the cause of micritized Calpionella, favouring inheritance from the source.
steps.quote: It can neither be generated by organisms such bacteria or algae, nor be linked to burial compaction

steps.action: Interprets the primary and post-depositional sedimentary structures as records of wave, storm, tidal and fluvial processes, and of subaerial exposure (desiccation cracks) and rapid deposition.
steps.quote: The primary sedimentary structures observed indicate erosion and deposition under the interplay of waves, storms, tidal and fluvial currents.

steps.action: Reassigns indicators usually read as deep-marine (flute and tool casts, Paleodictyon, Zoophycos) to fluvial-to-marine transition and shallow settings, citing literature occurrences, instead of accepting a deep-water reading.
steps.quote: Flute casts and tool casts are commonly linked to turbidity currents in deep marine settings. However they can form also in the fluvial-to-marine transition zone

steps.action: Groups the facies into a tide-dominated estuary association and a tide-dominated delta association, with their sub-environments.
steps.quote: The facies identified are grouped into three facies associations: Tide dominated estuary facies association, tide dominated delta facies association

steps.action: Chooses a prodelta over an offshore origin for facies F8 because F8 is associated with deltaic facies at the base of a coarsening-upward sequence.
steps.quote: This facies can be formed in an offshore or in a prodelta this last hypothesis is the most probable

steps.action: Interprets facies F18 to F22 as a sandy open-coast tidal flat, following the classification of Daidu (2012).
steps.quote: It corresponds to a sandy open coast tidal flat in the classification of Daidu (2012)

steps.action: Sets the petrographic result against the earlier siliciclastic description (Tejera de Leon 1993) and against mixed deposits reported elsewhere in the NW Rif.
steps.quote: the sediments are not siliciclastic deposits but rather mixed siliciclastic/carbonate components

steps.action: Checks the petrographic provenance inference against the independent paleocurrent data measured in this work (SSE to NNW transport).
steps.quote: This hypothesis is supported by the results of palaeocurrents analysis carried out in this work

steps.action: Sets the littoral to shallow-marine interpretation against the earlier deep-sea fan, slope and outer-platform interpretations.
steps.quote: Sedimentary facies reconstruction and interpretation performed in this work indicates that deposition of Mrayt Group sediments

steps.action: Explains the initiation of the Eocene estuary by valley drowning during the Ypresian sea-level rise, with subsidence and a warm humid climate, using cited global sea-level and climate curves.
steps.quote: The Mrayt Group estuary system was initiated by the drowning of an existing river valley

steps.action: Prefers non-deposition over erosion to explain the Mid-Upper Eocene gap, attributing it to eustatic fall and tectonic uplift.
steps.quote: could be explained by erosionor by an interruption in deposition.This last hypothesis seems the most plausible

steps.action: Takes from the literature the criteria that identify deltas and that separate tide-dominated deltas from other deltas and from other tidal settings (Galloway 1975; Goodbread and Saito 2012).
steps.quote: The criteria which serve to distinguish tide dominated delta from the other deltaic systems are

steps.action: Matches the Oligocene to Early Miocene succession against these delta criteria.
steps.quote: Recognition of tide dominated delta is alsobased on the typicalcriteria commonly admitted for delta identification

steps.action: Compares the delta flow direction from 48 flute casts with paleocurrents in earlier works, and notes deltaic systems reported in coeval NW Rif sections that were earlier read as deep-sea fans.
steps.quote: is consistent with that proposed by the previous works

steps.action: Explains delta development, three progradational units and the later open-coast tidal flat by tectonics, subsidence, eustasy, climate and sediment supply, correlated with cited curves (Haq et al. 1987; Zachos et al. 2001).
steps.quote: The initiation and the development of the Mrayt Group deltaswere favored by the combination of major factors

steps.action: Keeps the interpretation of an evolution from tide-dominated estuary to tide-dominated delta to open-coast tidal flat, under mixed fluvial, tidal, wave and storm processes and allogenic control.
steps.quote: The paleoenvironments of the Mrayt Group are interpreted as littoral andshallow marine settings

end.claim: The Mrayt Group was deposited in littoral and shallow-marine settings (tide-dominated estuary, then tide-dominated delta, then open-coast tidal flat), not in the deep-sea fan or slope settings proposed earlier.

decisive_move.sentence: Reading the sedimentary structures as tidal, wave, storm and fluvial signatures with subaerial exposure is what turns the facies descriptions into a littoral interpretation that opposes the deep-sea readings.

gates.evidence: The sections were logged and sampled descriptively; no stated hypothesis directed data acquisition. The interpretation could have failed had tidal and desiccation features been absent, but no explicit test against the rivals' predictions is reported, and deep-water indicators were reinterpreted rather than counted against the interpretation. Nothing was fixed before the data were seen.

imports.item: Identification of trace makers (decapod crustaceans, shrimps) used to read ichnofossil environments

limits: Only the supplied PDF (an EarthArXiv preprint) was coded. The acknowledgements thank an editor and two reviewers, but no review file was available, so no review sequence was coded. No point counts or percentages are reported for the Mount (1985) classification of the 50 thin sections. Which thin sections and samples represent which facies is not stated. Paleocurrent statistics are limited to a rose diagram; the Fig. 10 caption says SSE to NNE while the text says NNW. Ages are taken from earlier biostratigraphy, and no new dating was done. The rivals' predictions are not derived explicitly; deep-water indicators are accommodated by citing shallow occurrences (coded P), so the test against rivals is weak. The 'first time' claim for detailed sedimentology sits beside cited earlier sedimentological work (Raissouni et al. 2008; Tejera de Leon 1993). Sub-claims: mixed siliciclastic/carbonate composition is kept, close to an observation; provenance is best_explanation; allogenic controls (eustasy, climate, tectonics) are best_explanation, inferred by correlation with global curves, with no independent local constraint. Coding the outcome as contradicted is an inference: the paper argues the earlier deep-sea interpretations are wrong but does not run a decisive test.
